Step 5 directs the participant to send the arrest record, case disposition and motion to criminalmotionsealteam@dcsc.gov, the Superior Court Criminal Division Seal Team, which "gives the motion a case number and assigns it to a judge", with the Criminal Division clerk's office at 500 Indiana Avenue NW, Room 4001 named as the in-person alternative. FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: The packet carries, word for word, the sentence DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 names as its proven case: "Any filing fee or fee-waiver answer. No held source states a fee, that filing is free, or a waiver procedure - ask the Criminal Division clerk's office (202-879-1373) before filing." That is the standard's third met clause exactly: the packet states that no held source establishes the fee and names a specific checkable authority, an office with a street address (500 Indiana Avenue NW, Room 4001) and a telephone number. The committed track registry carries no fee for this track, so A1's "ask first whether the repository establishes the answer" is answered no, and the named authority properly stands in.

SERVICE.finding: Both halves are stated. Recipient: serve the prosecuting office after asking the Criminal Division clerk's office (202-879-1373) or the Seal Team which office prosecuted the case and its correct service address, with the two candidate offices named by name (the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia and the Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia). Method: the service page directs that the certificate be completed when the copy goes out in the manner the clerk directs. No held source states the routing rule between the two offices, so under DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001's extension to SERVICE the named, reachable authority stands in.

The profile's sourceFormStatements[7] ties this to the very form in this packet: "Petition and Order to Seal Arrest (Act 1460) — Arrest records under § 16-90-1409." On the petition the Signature of Petitioner rule and the Date rule are both blank on the boundary raster. The instructions state the rule affirmatively and then go further than most: 'The whole of the proposed order. PA-RCRIM-P-790-ORDER is the order the judge signs... Do not fill it in and do not sign it,' and the process-guidance page repeats it on the paper the participant is holding.

ARTIFACTS.detail: The render report is perfect and a second committed record in the same directory is not, so I score the obligation on both rather than only the convenient one. reports/rendered-artifacts.json is exact: I recomputed SHA-256 over every file it declares — two assembled 5-page packet PDFs and ten raster page PNGs — and got 12 declared digests, 12 matched, 0 mismatched, 0 missing, with declared byteLength and pageCount agreeing, and the two assembled fixtures are the exact bytes the central RASTER_PASS receipt binds. The failure is product-wiring.json. Its proposedRepresentation.components[0] names fixtures/canonical.pdf and declares sha256 4a7113112f29b05fdf21e6d6f6822d8ca41d3768c3ff2640cff72af6bbf308e0. That file computes to fb5024c3acb10682ac4e167fdcac4e83e6064b86293a7aa1eb602b97e12425af. 4a711311 is the pre-repair canonical, which the Vermont rebuild superseded; the record was not regenerated with the rest and now asserts a digest that is false about the bytes it names. The repair record disclosed this in terms rather than hiding it and left it for a Captain, which is the right posture — but a committed record carrying a false hash is a defect a repairer must close, not a note, so it is scored. Two lesser things, recorded as advisories rather than failures: the four per-document fixture PDFs on disk (canonical--PA-RCRIM-P-790-PETITION.pdf and its three siblings) are declared nowhere in the render report, so they are undeclared rather than misdeclared; and product-wiring.json's derivedFrom points at that same render report, so the two records disagree about the same file.
ARTIFACTS.repair: Regenerate product-wiring.json against the current render report so its declared canonical digest is fb5024c3ac..., or remove the digest if the wiring proposal does not need to pin one. Either way it must stop asserting 4a711311.

PAGE_ORDER.detail: Both fixtures declare a 5-page pageManifest running primary_filing (the petition), proposed_order across two pages (the order and its Rule 790 information page), then process_guidance across two pages, and the ten committed raster pages carry the same component label per page in the same order. That is the order the participant needs: the petition first, the order tendered with it, then the page that tells them whether they need to file at all. Reading the boundary pages in sequence shows it with no page misplaced, duplicated or missing — and the guidance page genuinely sits last, after the documents it discusses.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: Measured two ways. The central visual gate returned RASTER_PASS in run 33582245323, bound to the exact post-repair canonical and boundary digests I recomputed on disk, and that gate proves every page rendered, no page blank, expected dimensions at the requested scale, no clipped write, no overlapping participant text, no placeholder text and no protected-field ink. I also read the boundary raster directly. The boundary fixture stresses the form hard — 'Maria-Alejandra O'Shaughnessy-Whitfield' into the petition's Full Name cell, the v. caption and the order's petitioner line, and '1188 Upper Notch Crossing Road, Apartment 14B' into an address cell — and every one sits inside its cell with clear space, does not overrun the DOB cell to its right, and does not overprint the PETITIONER INFORMATION rules. Worth saying because it is the tell in this family's history: all ten raster PNGs are byte-identical across the Vermont repair, which is consistent with wrong-state text having lived in the composed instructions and the field map rather than on any rendered page.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Repaired, and repaired to the held answer rather than to a plausible one. The recorded failure was that the instructions sent a Pennsylvania petitioner to the Vermont Superior Court, Criminal Division. They now read: 'File the completed packet with the Clerk of Courts of the judicial district where the charges were disposed — the county named in the caption above. A Rule 790 expungement petition is decided by a judge of the Court of Common Pleas of that district, and it is decided there even if a magisterial district judge or a Philadelphia Municipal Court judge disposed of the case.' I checked that against the repository rather than accepting it: the committed track registry, track pa_pardon_expungement, holds destination.name 'Court of common pleas of the judicial district in which the charges were disposed' with the detail that on the fallback route the participant files the Rule 790 petition with the clerk of courts, and the national census carries the identical destination object. The instructions also tell the participant how to identify the district from the docket number and who can tell them. The process-guidance page carries the same destination on the paper, as it already did before the repair.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored under DETERMINATION_FEE_AND_WAIVER_STANDARD.json with A1 and A2 applied in order. Asking first whether the repository establishes the county figure across the whole A2 scope: it does not. src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/PA-pennsylvania.json — the shelf A2 was written about — has an empty packetGenerator.feeRules; the track registry's rules.fees says only 'No fee on the automatic route. County filing fees apply to the fallback petition and vary'; and no census requiredSourceId supplies a figure. What the repository does hold, it states: the registry's feeWaiver answer appears as 'Pennsylvania publishes statewide in forma pauperis forms for the Court of Common Pleas; this packet does not include one,' and the statewide range held in data/rcap-ledger/authority-ledger.json and session-a-evidence-packet.json appears as 'roughly $132 to $215 ... treat that as a range to expect, not as your county's figure' — presented as a range, attributed as reported, and explicitly not passed off as the participant's number. Where the record is genuinely empty the packet takes the standard's third limb and names a specific reachable authority: 'Ask the Clerk of Courts of the judicial district where the charges were disposed for the current fee,' and the same office for how to file in forma pauperis. That is the whole obligation met — the participant can find out what filing costs, is told what is known, and is not handed an invented county figure.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.advisory: One held sentence is not carried: the registry's 'No fee on the automatic route.' The instructions do tell the participant that on the automatic route 'there is nothing here to file', from which nothing-to-pay follows, and the process-guidance page says the same, so the participant is not left uncertain. But A1's ordering would have it stated, and stating it costs one clause. Recorded for the repairer that has to open this family anyway.

evidence.namedCheckableAuthority: Clerk of Courts of the judicial district where the charges were disposed

SERVICE.detail: Repaired, and to an answer that was on the packet's own paper the whole time. The recorded failure was that the instructions sent service questions to a Vermont clerk and told the participant to get a Vermont State's Attorney to sign a stipulation the packet does not contain. That is gone — 'State's Attorney' occurs zero times in the family now. The instructions state: 'After you file, the petition is served on the Commonwealth — the District Attorney, as the attorney for the Commonwealth — and the Commonwealth then has 60 days from service to consent, object, or do nothing,' followed by what happens after that window and the 30-day stay on an order granted without consent, and 'Keep your proof of service with your copy of the packet.' Three independent held records agree: the delivered petition prints 'When this petition is filed with the Clerk of Courts, the petitioner shall serve a copy upon the attorney for the Commonwealth' on its own face, which I read off the boundary raster; the track registry's rules.service says service on the attorney for the Commonwealth on the fallback route and none on the automatic route; and its rules.notice carries the 60-day Rule 790 response window. Nothing here rests on a named authority standing in for a missing rule, because the rule is not missing.

evidence.heldAt: legal-design-track-registry.json track pa_pardon_expungement rules.service and rules.notice

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Repaired. The recorded failure was that the stop language existed but described the wrong state's packet — 'a prepared set of official Vermont forms' and 'whether the court will seal the record' on a Pennsylvania expungement family. It now reads 'This is a prepared set of official Pennsylvania forms — the statewide Pa.R.Crim.P. 790 petition and blank expungement order — and a process-guidance page. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will order expungement.' Both halves are now true of what the participant is holding: the forms are the two AOPC Rule 790 documents and the relief is expungement. The same stop is printed on the paper, as the closing section of the process-guidance page. This family also does something better than most: the guidance page opens with 'READ THIS BEFORE YOU FILE ANYTHING' and tells the participant that if the automatic route has already cleared the record there is nothing here to file, on the stated ground that a packet which only ever told you to file would be telling you to do work you may not need to do and to pay for it. And it refuses to state a timetable or a criterion it cannot source, saying so in terms. That is a real stop, not a disclaimer.
SELF_HELP_STOP.advisory: The committed track registry holds three named selfHelpStopConditions for this track that the packet does not carry as such: the participant has not yet obtained a pardon, the pardon application itself being out of scope and a referral; whether the pardon is conditional or unconditional cannot be determined from the document; and the record still appearing after the quarterly cycle with the fallback route's availability unclear. The instructions do address the second in substance, distinguishing unconditional from conditional and leaving the determination to the participant, and the guidance page addresses the third in substance. The first — that this packet presupposes a pardon already granted and that the pardon application is a referral — I could not find stated anywhere. Recorded as a Captain's question in the same terms as the Kentucky families, since the same boundary is in play across many families.

I searched this family's entire output for that figure and for the string 1203.4 and found neither, in any text artifact or in any of the 16 delivered PDFs. COMPONENT_SET.detail: Two related failures, one in the binding and one in what the guidance component actually contains. The committed registry declares three components for this packetSet: pa_pardon_expungement-process-guidance-1, requirement 'required'; -primary-filing-2, requirement 'conditional'; and -proposed-order-3, requirement 'conditional'. product-wiring.json binding.packetComponents names the two conditional ones and omits the required one. That is exactly inverted, and it matters here more than it would elsewhere: the guidance page is the only artifact in the packet that serves pa_pardon_automatic_route, so a binding without it represents a two-route family as a one-route one and drops the route on which nothing is filed at all. Second, the registry's own description of what that component is for reads 'The guidance explains the quarterly cycle and how to verify the record cleared.' I extracted the rendered guidance page from fixtures/canonical.pdf: it explains how to verify, by asking the Clerk of Courts what the docket now shows, but it never mentions the Board of Pardons, the AOPC or the quarterly cycle, and it says in terms 'This page states no timetable and no criterion for that.' The component is present and rendered but under-delivers the one thing the registry assigns it. Note that the delivered set is otherwise complete and correctly declared: production-field-map.json componentSet and rendered-artifacts.json componentSet both list all three.
COMPONENT_SET.evidence: product-wiring.json binding.packetComponents; registry packetSet.components and units for trackId pa_pardon_expungement; guidance page text extracted from fixtures/canonical.pdf pages 4-5; production-field-map.json componentSet

KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: The seventeen writes themselves are sound - I read every one of them back out of the finalized bytes and all twenty-eight write records across both fixtures have drawnText exactly equal to expected, each bound to a factId and to a widget rect read from the pinned binary. The failure is that participant-instructions.md misdescribes them to the participant. Its opening sentence reads: 'The platform filled in what it holds about you: your name, your date of birth, your address, your telephone number, your email and your docket number.' It did not fill in a telephone number or an email, and could not have: I enumerated all 109 terminal field entries across both official forms and the composed guidance document and none of them is a telephone or email field, and none of the seventeen writes carries a phone or email factId. The sentence tells a participant that two categories of their data were placed on these forms when no such blank exists on either form. It is the mirror image of what DET-FEE-AND-WAIVER-001 A4 forbids - a packet asserting about itself something that is not so - and the same integrity rule reaches it. The sentence is shared boilerplate: seven census-v1 families carry it, so the repair here is to make this family's sentence name only what this family writes, which is name, date of birth, street address, city, state, ZIP, county and docket number.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The repository answers it and the packet states it, for both routes. The registry gives venue 'The court of common pleas of the judicial district in which the charges were disposed' and destination detail 'On the automatic route the Board of Pardons and the AOPC deliver the record to the court and nothing is filed. On the fallback route the participant files the Rule 790 petition with the clerk of courts and serves the attorney for the Commonwealth.' participant-instructions.md says to file with the Clerk of Courts of the judicial district where the charges were disposed, that a judge of the Court of Common Pleas of that district decides it, and - a real addition rather than a restatement - that it is decided there even if a magisterial district judge or a Philadelphia Municipal Court judge disposed of the case. It also tells a participant who does not know their district that the docket number identifies it and the Clerk of Courts can tell them from it, which is a checkable office rather than a shrug. The guidance page repeats the destination for the fallback route and states that nothing is filed on the automatic one.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Scored against A1 to A4 and it holds. The registry answers both facts for this route: rules.fees 'No fee on the automatic route. County filing fees apply to the fallback petition and vary' and rules.feeWaiver 'In forma pauperis relief is available for the fallback petition.' The packet states both. On the fee it says Pennsylvania fees are set county by county and no held source states the fee for the participant's county - which is what the record says, not a denial of a held answer - and then does better than a shrug by giving the range the repository actually holds. I checked that range against its source rather than accepting it: data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/PA.memo.json carries 'County filing fees vary and are not established by statute. The legal review reports a range of roughly $132 to $215 across counties, with expungement petitions generally costing more than limited access petitions. No confirmed statewide schedule exists', and the packet reproduces it with the same hedge and tells the participant to treat it as a range to expect rather than as their county's figure, and to ask the Clerk of Courts. On the waiver it states that in forma pauperis relief exists, that Pennsylvania publishes statewide IFP forms for the Court of Common Pleas, that this packet does not include one, and which office can tell them how to file that way - a disclosed absence, not a concealed one. A3 check performed deliberately because the figure invited it: the same $132 appears elsewhere in the repository as New Mexico's district-court filing fee in NM.memo.json, so I confirmed the PA range has its own Pennsylvania source and is not a sibling jurisdiction's answer read across. It is not. Only gap, recorded and not failed: the registry's 'No fee on the automatic route' is not stated in those words, though the packet twice tells the participant there is nothing to file on that route.
FEE_AND_WAIVER.evidence: registry rules.fees and rules.feeWaiver; participant-instructions.md 'What filing costs'; data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/PA.memo.json fees and openQuestions; NM.memo.json checked to rule out a cross-jurisdiction read

SERVICE.detail: The repository answers it and the packet states it in more detail than the record required. Registry rules.service: 'None on the automatic route; service on the attorney for the Commonwealth on the fallback route.' rules.notice adds the 60-day response window under Rule 790. participant-instructions.md tells the participant that after filing the petition is served on the Commonwealth - the District Attorney, as the attorney for the Commonwealth - that the Commonwealth then has 60 days from service to consent, object or do nothing, that after that window the judge grants, denies or schedules a hearing, that an order granted without the Commonwealth's consent is stayed for 30 days while an appeal may be taken, and to keep proof of service with the packet copy. The order's own field asking which criminal justice agencies are to be served with the order is carried through to the participant as an item to supply. Nothing here is read across from a sibling route: the automatic route is separately described as involving no participant filing and no service.
SERVICE.evidence: registry rules.service and rules.notice; participant-instructions.md 'After you file' paragraph; production-field-map.json order field 'Criminal justice agencies to be served with the order'

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: The registry holds three selfHelpStopConditions for trackId pa_pardon_expungement and the packet carries none of them as a stop. First: 'The participant has not yet obtained a pardon; the pardon application itself is out of scope and is a referral.' I grepped every participant-facing surface in this family - participant-instructions.md and the rendered guidance pages of both fixtures - and nothing anywhere tells a reader who does not yet hold a pardon that this packet is not for them and that applying for one is out of scope and a referral. The packet presupposes the pardon throughout and never says what to do if the premise fails. Second: 'Whether the pardon is conditional or unconditional cannot be determined from the document.' The instructions mention the distinction and say a conditional pardon may lead to Clean Slate limited access rather than expungement, but they never state the stop - that where the document does not settle which kind it is, self-help ends. Third: 'The record still appears after the quarterly cycle and the fallback route's availability is unclear.' The guidance page states the opposite of a stop: 'If the record is already clear, stop; if it is not, file the petition.' It then declines the criterion the stop is keyed to, saying 'This page states no timetable and no criterion for that, because neither is established by the two forms this packet is built from.' That reasoning scopes the question to the two official forms, but A1 and A2 scope it to the repository, and the repository answers it: the registry's own unit description records the quarterly Board of Pardons to AOPC transmission and says of this very component that 'The guidance explains the quarterly cycle and how to verify the record cleared.' The packet's own participant-instructions.md states the quarterly cycle in terms. So the guidance page tells a participant it states no timetable while the packet states one two files away - the sentence A4 forbids. The repair is to carry the three stop conditions onto the participant-facing surface and to let the guidance page state the quarterly cycle it is chartered to state.
SELF_HELP_STOP.evidence: registry selfHelpStopConditions and units[0].description for trackId pa_pardon_expungement; guidance page text extracted from fixtures/canonical.pdf and fixtures/boundary.pdf; participant-instructions.md step 4; grep for pardon, board, quarter, referral across the family's participant-facing surfaces

COMPONENT_SET.finding: The delivered packet contains an official-PDF component the route does not name, and the committed records single that component out as one that must not reach a participant. The registry's packetSet for wv_conv_single_misdemeanor-set names five components: primary_filing, verification and certificate_of_service, all three on SCA-C906, plus service_package and filing_instructions, both process_guidance with officialFormId null. The packet nonetheless binds the whole of SCA-C900 as packet pages 5 to 9, and pages 6 to 9 are its embedded petition, verification and certificate of service — a second, complete, blank petition sitting directly behind the correct one. Read out of the delivered bytes, that embedded petition carries the repealed pre-2019 law the registry's release blocker enumerates: page 6 states 'was between eighteen and twenty-six years of age' and 'have no prior or subsequent convictions other than minor traffic violations', and cross-references exclusions to 'W. Va. Code §61-11-26(i)', a subsection the section in force no longer uses. Separately, delivered page 5 prints 'you will be notified and will then have ten (10) days of being served of such notice to reply', and the committed authority decision NATIONAL-2026-08-28-C-WV-02 records in terms that 'The reply period after an opposition is thirty days under subsection (g)(3), not the ten days the SCA-C900 instruction sheet prints against subsection (e).' So the packet states a reply deadline on its own face that this repository's own authority record says is wrong, on a once-per-lifetime remedy.

SERVICE.finding: Who must be served, and how, is stated and matches the statute the registry cites. FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Both are stated, and the packet does something careful with a trap that would be easy to get wrong. It reports the $150 fee the compiled profile records, quoting it verbatim — '§ 99-19-72 sets a $150 filing fee for each petition to expunge an offense under 99-19-71' — and then states plainly, in capitals, that this petition is brought under § 99-15-26(5) and not under § 99-19-71. It does not stop at the distinction: it notes that the same profile records the operative expungement provision as appearing in both § 99-15-26(5) and § 99-19-71(4), says no record it binds settles whether the § 99-19-72 fee reaches a petition under § 99-15-26(5), and refuses to decide it in either direction — while telling the participant to expect to be asked for $150 and to ask the clerk's office what that court charges before going, 'because a filing you cannot pay for is a filing you cannot make'. On the waiver it says no record it binds states one and names the same clerk's office as the office that answers. That is the fee and the waiver route stated as far as the record reaches, with the reasoning shown.

SERVICE.finding: Who must be served, and how, is not answerable from any committed record. The route contract at routes[13] of src/lib/legal-authority/routes/mississippi.json carries no service field, no notice field and no proof-of-service field — the question is not recorded as unresolved, it is simply not addressed anywhere in the record this route has. The packet states exactly that: 'No committed record this packet binds states who must be served on this route, or how. The office that answers it is the clerk's office of the Mississippi court that granted nonadjudication and entered the dismissal or closure order.' That is the honest thing to print, and it is not an answer to this obligation. It is recorded as blocked rather than as a pass because the packet does not say who must be served, and rather than as a failure because no repairer can supply from this repository an answer the repository does not hold.

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: The packet states where self-help ends, and every stop it prints is traceable to the record it binds. Its five conditions are: still on nonadjudication or no dismissal or closure order entered, which is the contract's timing anchor read as a stop; prior use of nonadjudication, which is the contract's 'Once only'; a DUI, implied-consent or trafficking element, which is the contract's third exclusion; a court level the contract records as excluded, which is its first; and any immigration question. The route contract declares no selfHelpBoundaries list of its own, so these are composed from its exclusions and its timing rather than copied from a list, and nothing the contract records as an exclusion is missing.

contractExclusions: No trafficking, implied-consent, or DUI misuse
evidence.observationNotScored: The compiled Mississippi profile — which this family also binds as authority — carries, at ruleClauses[13] of its nonadjudication-under-99-15-26 pathway and immediately after that pathway's own mechanism description, the sentence 'This may apply in felony and misdemeanor cases, but there are exclusions, especially crimes against the person, crimes of violence, and certain public corruption/abuse-of-office offenses.' None of violence, 'against the person', corruption or 'abuse of office' appears anywhere in this packet or its participant-instructions.md; all four return 0 hits. This lane did NOT score that a failure, and the reason is stated so the Captain can weigh it rather than take it on trust: that pathway record is demonstrably an aggregation across sections — its summary and its structured exclusionRules field are both plainly about the § 99-19-71 felony route, naming the general felony waiting period and the public-official bar — so a clause inside it is weaker authority than the route contract, which is the record the census marks as superseding and whose three exclusions the packet carries in full. It is recorded here because the omitted classes are serious ones and because the packet's own item C2 asks the participant 'What is the offense and does an exclusion apply?' without telling them which exclusions to check against.
